name: jsonlong
algorithm: Each language's std JSON on one array of long strings built in the program from splitmix64(seed), byte for byte the same in every language: parse it reps times and sum the decoded string lengths, or parse it once and write it as compact JSON reps times and sum the lengths (README.md).

skip.c: no std JSON: C has no standard JSON parser or writer; no library stands in
skip.rust: no std JSON: Rust std has none (serde_json is a crate); no crate stands in
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; the checksum (decoded or written lengths) checks that every library read or wrote the same strings
notes: The document is about 1.2 MB: 2,000 strings of 100 to 1,099 bytes of printable ASCII without a quote or a backslash, with an escape (backslash n, or backslash quote) about every 256 bytes. parse sums the decoded string lengths over reps parses; write parses once and sums the formatted lengths over reps formats.

Idiomatic standard library (plan/06-m6.md 4.1): Mk json.Parse into an arena Reset per rep, and Value.Format into a Text cleared per rep; Go encoding/json Unmarshal into any, and an Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) into a bytes.Buffer reset per rep (the trailing newline not counted); Zig std.json.parseFromSliceLeaky into std.json.Value in an ArenaAllocator reset per rep, and std.json.Stringify.valueAlloc. Every language builds the document inside its timed run.
